ko.executive_summary: AI optical interconnect speeds are scaling from 800G to 1.6T, making thermoelectric cooling (TEC) a critical thermal management component in the supply chain. PhotonicX AI secured $21.8M Series A funding at $266M valuation to advance optical chip capabilities, while Japan's JERA engages with major AI players (Anthropic, Meta) on data center infrastructure.
key_facts: PhotonicX AI Series A: $21.8M at $266M valuation
JERA (Japan) negotiating with Anthropic and Meta
Thermoelectric cooling (TEC) identified as supply chain critical component

implications.text: TEC adoption becomes essential as optical transceiver densities and power consumption increase from 800G to 1.6T speeds, creating new supply chain dependencies.
PhotonicX AI's $266M valuation signals strong investor confidence in integrated photonics for AI, expanding the competitive landscape beyond traditional optical transceiver vendors.
JERA's engagement with Anthropic and Meta indicates Japan's utility/infrastructure providers are positioning for AI data center buildout, potentially shifting optical component sourcing geographies.

ko.counterpoint: Limited visibility into TEC supplier capacity and standardization roadmap at higher transceiver speeds; JERA discussions remain preliminary with no announced commitments or timelines.
